test_cases.expected_output: Scans existing notes for two distinct outputs, presented separately: (a) mechanical link suggestions — two related but unlinked notes, presented as a batch for the user to approve/reject together, then recorded as a link and a [[wikilink]]; (b) sparked ideas — a genuinely new synthesis noticed between existing notes, not stated in either alone, recorded as an Evergreen candidate for later make-evergreen-note grounding, never auto-written as a note itself.

test_cases.prompt: find-connections where two notes are related but already linked
test_cases.expected_output: Does not re-suggest the existing link — checks .slipbox/bin/slipbox links find before proposing a candidate.
No --references or --evergreen flag was given. Stops and asks the user which mode they mean instead of guessing or defaulting to one — per the explicit mode-flag requirement in SKILL.md.

Scans Reference/Person/Location/Organization recurrence only — mechanical link suggestions and sparked ideas are out of scope for this mode. Every candidate crossing threshold is batch-presented, never auto-written; for any approved Reference candidate the user is told to invoke /make-reference-note themselves.

Scans for mechanical link suggestions and sparked ideas only — Reference/Person/Location/Organization recurrence is out of scope for this mode. Approved links get both a links row and inline wikilink written; sparked ideas are routed to the evergreen backlog via slipbox evergreen add, never written as a note directly.

test_cases.prompt: find-connections --references where [[UI Design]] appears once in one literature note and [[User Interface Design]] appears once in a different literature note
test_cases.expected_output: Semantic clustering runs before threshold-counting: [[UI Design]] and [[User Interface Design]] are recognized as variant labels for the same underlying thing and clustered together first. The cluster's combined count (one mention each, two total) crosses the 2+ recurrence threshold as a single candidate, surfaced with both labels listed as alt_names — neither label alone would reach 2+ under exact-string counting, so counting before clustering would have missed this case entirely.

test_cases.prompt: find-connections --references where a wikilink target recurs across notes and turns out to be a person's name
test_cases.expected_output: Entity exclusion runs before the Admission sequence: a vault-wide, folder-agnostic filename lookup checks whether a Person/Location/Organization note already exists for this name, with no paths.* config involved. Once identified as a Person candidate, it is batch-presented the same way a Reference candidate would be (recurrence threshold met, shown with its source notes) but find-connections never attempts to write it — no Person note gets created, and no make-literature-note/make-reference-note invocation happens on this entity's behalf.

test_cases.prompt: find-connections --references where a candidate appears in a source-map cache but was not retained in any final Literature note
test_cases.expected_output: Does not surface the cached candidate. Caches may verify a selected candidate only; discovery reads final Literature Key Concepts, Mentioned, and relevant retained prose.

test_cases.prompt: find-connections --references where two variant labels recur but one source-specific label lacks independent support
test_cases.expected_output: Clusters labels before counting, then applies the ordered admission sequence. The unresolved candidate is reported without invoking a title-shape test.

test_cases.prompt: find-connections --references where a candidate recurs in three Literature notes but all three notes trace to one duplicated source
test_cases.expected_output: Reports the recurrence cluster as unresolved because recurrence does not establish warrant and the duplicated notes provide only one independent support path; leaves every wikilink untouched and creates no provisional Reference artifact or work_id.

test_cases.prompt: find-connections --references where a recurring candidate is approved but one contributing source has no grounded Literature note
test_cases.expected_output: Presents the candidate in the read-only batch, then directs the user to make-literature-note for the ungrounded source before make-reference-note; it creates no Reference artifact during discovery.

test_cases.prompt: find-connections --references where a recurring cluster is a tool, event, or creative work rather than an abstract concept
test_cases.expected_output: Reports the cluster as a Reference candidate when the ordered admission gates pass, showing alt_names, recurrence count, and source notes; it remains batch-presented and the user invokes make-reference-note themselves.

test_cases.prompt: find-connections --evergreen finds a spark between Notes/Spacing.md and Notes/Compounding.md
test_cases.expected_output: Records an Evergreen candidate through /using-slipbox with origin_kind note-connection and both exact scanned vault-relative paths in origin_paths.
